title: Search visibility & growth plan
label: ILLUSTRATIVE REPORT TEMPLATE
subtitle: SEO / AI search / reputation
summary: A clear view of the business, the evidence that matters and the next actions. This fictional example demonstrates the report layout; it does not describe an inspected client or establish search performance.

sections.title: The executive perspective
sections.lead: Make the offer easier to understand, the proof easier to check and the next step easier to take.

blocks.text: A useful search strategy begins with the customer. Establish what the business sells, identify the questions that influence a buying decision, and connect each recommendation to a page and a measurable outcome.

blocks.source: Fictional example for the report template. These values are illustrative, not measurements of a real website.

blocks.title: The decision
blocks.text: Start with the service journey and credible project evidence. Expand publishing after the destination pages give prospective customers a useful next step.

blocks.title: Three priorities
items: Explain the offer: who it is for, what the engagement includes and how to start.
Make proof inspectable: connect project claims to attributable sources and clear limitations.
Measure the same questions and pages again; separate implementation progress from actual search outcomes.

sections.title: Business & research scope
sections.lead: Understand the company before choosing who to compare it with.

rows: Inspect main service and implementation pages.
Check sales context, case studies and owner instructions.
Keep office location, delivery market and website language separate.
Record browser, provider, query, date and actual coverage.

blocks.title: Read coverage before conclusions
blocks.text: A failed request does not establish missing content. An incomplete render does not establish missing schema. Record the limitation and continue with the evidence that can be inspected.

The final client report should identify the homepage, About, Contact, service and proof pages actually inspected. Keep uninspected areas visible rather than presenting a sampled crawl as a complete inventory.

sections.title: Buyer language & page intent
sections.lead: Use the language of a buying decision, then check the results.

rows: Which agency can automate customer support?
How much does a small automation project cost?
How will our team manage the system after launch?
blocks.source: Illustrative wording. Demand, difficulty and ranking are unmeasured.

blocks.title: Turn a question into a useful answer
blocks.text: State the short answer first. Explain what changes the answer, give a relevant example, name the evidence and show the next step. Avoid turning every phrase variation into a separate page.

A research query helps discover useful pages. A recommended keyword needs a business-fit explanation, an appropriate destination and a verification plan. Search-result presence alone does not establish demand.

sections.title: A fair competitor comparison
sections.lead: Compare similar offers and customer needs. Label differences that matter.

rows: Comparable services, buyers and specific markets
Offer detail, implementation process and attributable proof
Useful customer experience patterns; separate market context
blocks.source: Reserved fictional domains. No business identity, rank or authority claim is made.

blocks.title: Fewer strong comparisons are more useful
blocks.text: Inspect a broader candidate pool and aim for five supported direct competitors. If only two qualify, report two. Directories, publishers and software products do not become agencies because their pages share a keyword.

blocks.title: The comparison contract
items: Show exact supporting pages and capture dates.
Explain services, markets, comparability and important differences.
Retain confidence, evidence gaps and concise rejection reasons.

sections.title: Reputation built on evidence
sections.lead: Discover the leads. Verify the source pages. Compare like-for-like research.

blocks.text: Begin with the browser the agent actually controls. Try permitted Google navigation, then available host search and native discovery fallbacks. Keep the website audit running when search is restricted.

blocks.title: An unknown is not a weak result
blocks.text: Unread sources remain unknown. Unequal query coverage, dates, providers or source checks can prevent a numerical position. The report should still explain observed strengths, gaps and next actions.

sections.title: Findings with an acceptance check
sections.lead: Every recommendation should be something the client can inspect and verify.

blocks.title: Explain the implementation journey
blocks.observation: Illustrative finding: the supplied fictional service outline lists capabilities but does not explain the stages of an engagement.
blocks.impact: A prospective buyer needs to understand scope, involvement, delivery and handover before starting a conversation.
blocks.action: Add a short section covering discovery, scope agreement, build, review, handover and ongoing support. Use the actual delivery process and avoid invented time or cost promises.
blocks.rationale: Addresses a customer decision at the main service destination. Confirm the gap through a complete capture before implementation.
blocks.acceptance: Inspect the full page, confirm the gap, publish approved factual copy and recrawl. A reader should be able to explain the next step and their role in the project.

blocks.title: Readiness and visibility are separate
blocks.text: Readable content, coherent entities, useful answers and appropriate schema improve the quality of the source. They do not prove that an AI engine has cited or will cite the website.

sections.lead: Sequence the work so that each stage supports the next.

blocks.title: A publishing plan with a purpose
blocks.text: Use the BeyondSEO library to qualify 15 or 20 sources for the actual business. For each, specify the venue, article or contribution, target page, posting steps, eligibility, current terms and a realistic date. Do not fill the list with irrelevant websites.

blocks.title: Built for the next decision
blocks.text: A strong report explains what was observed, why it matters, what to do and how to check the result. BeyondSEO keeps those decisions connected to their evidence.
